title: DSH trusted-local acceptance specification (Windows, no sandbox)

supersedes.note: This file does NOT modify or replace qualification/specs/acceptance-spec.json. The old spec stays on disk, immutable, as history. This is a NEW spec under a NEW deployment identity.

trust_model.name: trusted-local
trust_model.one_line: The OS user account is the execution authority boundary.
trust_model.statement: DSH runs as the invoking Windows user with no sandbox, no WSL, no Linux VM and no SSH execution world. Every process it starts -- including the IPython kernel -- runs as that same OS user with that user's full filesystem, network and process visibility. This deployment therefore claims NO confinement of reads, writes, network or process visibility, and no case in this spec may be read as establishing one. What this deployment does claim is bounded and checkable: identity, composition, one programmable execution surface, correct data and recovery behaviour, bounded concurrency, honest verification, and research provenance.
explicitly_not_claimed: host-secret read isolation (any process can read any file the OS user can read)
network / egress isolation (there is no OS or gateway boundary)
filesystem write confinement (danger-full-access means no write restriction either)
a second execution world, and therefore any cross-world path consistency or role transition
verification-environment privilege separation from the host
trust_model.sandbox_rows_retained_because: The pinned DSH ABI requires them. `sandboxPolicy` is a SERVICE that seven entries inject, and `inject` is a readiness gate: deleting the row leaves those entries permanently pending, cascades so that shell/fs/ptcRuntime never publish, and the preset fails to mount with the model's tool face at ZERO. MEASURED. The rows are therefore configured as `danger-full-access`, which is DSH's own first-class path (ConfinedSandboxMode EXCLUDES it by type).
trust_model.identity_boundary: compatibility.lock.json -> deployment.identity. Every case below is bound to that identity. A PASS recorded against another identity is not a PASS for this one.

layer_legend.T0: pure function / type level; no DSH service involved
layer_legend.T1: production DSH services with a mock provider
layer_legend.T2: the actual built host / profile / preset, booted
layer_legend.T3: real subprocess kill and real disk recovery

layer_legend.T6: a real coding or research task end to end

case_shape.id: family prefix + 2-digit ordinal, unique across this file
case_shape.requirement: the invariant this case is about, as a short noun phrase
case_shape.stimulus: the exact thing an operator does to the system
case_shape.oracle: the observation that decides PASS. It states what is OBSERVED, and names the failure case, so a reader can falsify it without asking the author.
case_shape.layer: one of the layer_legend keys; the tier the verdict is allowed to be claimed at
case_shape.mandatory: true for every case in this file
case_shape.evidence: always [] at authoring time; a PASS requires at least one local evidence record with a sha256

mandatory_rule: Every case in this file is mandatory. NOT_APPLICABLE is not available to any case here; the only cases in this spec that are out of scope are recorded in not_applicable_inherited, which is not a case list.
no_inheritance_rule: NO PASS IS INHERITED. Not one case below carries a status or an evidence entry copied from the old 104-case report or the old 112-case spec. The old 85 PASSes remain valid evidence for the OLD deployment identity only. A case here is PASS only when it has its own evidence file, recorded under THIS identity, and that file establishes this oracle.

families.name: IDENTITY
families.subject: What this deployment IS. Artifact identity, spec identity, and the rule that no old verdict migrates.

families.name: COMPOSITION
families.subject: How the host profile and agent preset are assembled, including the retained sandbox rows at danger-full-access and the real model-visible tool surface.

families.name: IPYTHON
families.subject: The persistent IPython kernel as the PRIMARY programmable execution surface: real shell, persistent namespace, one tool with one parameter, host-owned lifecycle, bounded output, visible epochs.

families.name: NATIVE BRIDGE
families.subject: The path from a Python cell to a native DSH tool: one shared policy pipeline, dynamic revocation, reference delivery, no forged host facts, bounded nesting.

families.name: DATA
families.subject: Capture, paging, integrity and gap attribution for observations and artifacts, including the model-visible projection bound.

families.name: RECOVERY
families.subject: Crash, kill, stale-epoch and hostile-checkpoint behaviour; unknown outcomes stay unknown.

families.name: FILESYSTEM
families.subject: Filesystem behaviour under trusted-local. These cases check CORRECTNESS and HONEST DISCLOSURE, never confinement -- there is no confinement to check.

families.name: CONCURRENCY
families.subject: The hard child capacity, all admission paths, real top-up, unknown occupancy, root non-starvation and credit atomicity.

families.name: VERIFICATION
families.subject: Verification integrity: zero tests, skips, oracle tampering, receipt freshness, A-B-A, in-flight writers, tier honesty.
families.numbering_warning: RE-ISSUED NUMBERING. This spec's VER-01..09 are NEW cases and do NOT inherit the old spec's VER-01..09. In particular this VER-04 (receipt freshness) is NOT the old VER-04 (host execution bypass); the old VER-04 is out of scope by architecture decision and is recorded in not_applicable_inherited under its old id. Do not file evidence for one against the other.

families.name: RESEARCH
families.subject: Search-to-citation provenance: real sources, evidence tiers, incomplete parses, truncation, raw/derived separation, claim location.

families.name: CACHE/OBSERVABILITY
families.subject: Observation caching, history watermarks and the three separate visibilities (obtainable / consumed / model-projected).

cases.requirement: no silent degradation to danger-full-access
cases.stimulus: Remove the sandbox provider row(s) and boot, then separately boot the normal configuration and read `defaultMode`, any session override, and `resolve().mode`.
cases.oracle: With the provider missing, the loader FAILS with an explicit error naming the missing provider and does NOT boot with an unwrapped argv or an implicit danger-full-access. In the normal boot the three values are separately observable, and the deployment default is recorded as EXPLICITLY CONFIGURED rather than a fallback. A boot that cannot distinguish an explicitly configured danger-full-access from a provider-missing fallback is NOT PASS.

evidence.note: Gate row CMP-03. FAILURE DIRECTION, measured: with the sandbox provider rows disabled the loader FAILS EXPLICITLY -- "dsh: warning: 4 entries did not activate" plus RemoteError: agent-presets: preset "daily-standard" failed to mount: 2 row(s) did not activate, and the missing provider is NAMED per row (ptc-runtime pending waiting for services: sandbox, sandboxPolicy; terminal-controller, workspace-files, ui-deliverables pending waiting for service: sandboxPolicy). toolCount 0. No unwrapped argv and no implicit danger-full-access: a silent fallback would have produced a POPULATED tool face.

LIMIT recorded in GATES.md section 4: the product CANNOT distinguish an explicitly configured default from a fallback (modeSource is "unobservable" by the guard's own module header), and the measured composed row shows the deployment never configured the mode at all.

cases.oracle: Both reads SUCCEED and the record states that reads are not confined. A read-only mount must not be presented as secrecy, and a documentation claim of read isolation is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: one path string resolves to one file in one world
cases.stimulus: Resolve the same path string through a native `read`, a `grep`, a spawned process and a Python cell.
cases.oracle: All four resolve in the SAME execution world and reach the same file; the record names that world. Any mixed resolution, where one route reads a different file than another, is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: link and rename behaviour is recorded per vector, including where nothing refuses
cases.stimulus: Attempt a symlink escape, a hardlink creation and a cross-boundary rename.
cases.oracle: Each vector's observed outcome is recorded separately, and a vector that is NOT refused is reported as a finding rather than folded into a green. The correctness half must hold in every case: no data corruption, and no operation silently acting on a different file than the caller named.

cases.requirement: structured file tools keep their documented semantics
cases.stimulus: `read` a large file with offset and limit; `edit` an exact unique replacement; attempt an ambiguous replacement.
cases.oracle: Pagination returns the requested window, the exact replacement applies once, and the ambiguous case is refused rather than guessing. These tools remain usable beside the Python path rather than being degraded to decoration.

cases.requirement: workspace files and store-owned artifacts are not conflated
cases.stimulus: List what a cell can reach in the workspace and what the artifact store owns, then write a workspace file with the same name as an artifact.
cases.oracle: The record distinguishes workspace paths from store-owned artifacts, and the store's object is unaffected by the workspace write. Assuming an artifact is immutable merely because a cell can write a same-named path is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: the hard capacity of 30 is never exceeded
cases.stimulus: With 30 valid children occupying slots, request a 31st and a 32nd.
cases.oracle: Both requests are refused BEFORE publication, and the occupancy counter never exceeds 30 at any sampled instant. The refusal code and the observed high-water mark are recorded.

evidence.what: The admit/refuse boundary at target 10 and cap 30: 30 occupied, the 31st and 32nd refused with code HOST_CAPACITY_REACHED, highWater 30, headroom 20. One test, exit 0.
REAL N=10: ten distinct children in flight through the real continuable seam, the 11th refused at the target, the root holds no slot, highWater 10.

The composed-profile boot: the ledger limit is the deployment constant 30, a real child through the model-facing seam moved it 0 -> 1, and at the boundary a genuine startContinuable was REFUSED with "hard capacity is 30", occupancy never above 30.
The 19/19 verdict over that boot, with the probe digest and the deployment identity recorded alongside it.
The whole capacity.test.ts file in one run: 41 passed | 1 expected fail (42), exit 0.

cases.note: PASS. Two arms, deliberately different instruments: the boundary is reached ARITHMETICALLY on the deployment s own ledger (29 synthetic reservations plus the boundary calls), and the bindingness of the boundary is measured on a REAL composed-profile boot, where a genuine startContinuable call was refused at 30 with the message naming the deployment constant. No 30 real children were spawned, per the operator s CPU constraint.

cases.requirement: every admission path shares one quota
cases.stimulus: Request slots through a one-shot start, a continuable start, a workflow, a direct factory and a cold resume.
cases.oracle: All paths draw on the same host-wide quota, and a large caller-supplied `maxDepth` cannot bypass the ceiling. A path that admits without consulting the quota is NOT PASS.

evidence.what: Four creation paths each take a host slot through the real registry: continuable, one-shot, direct AgentFactory and workflow/PTC; a non-child session fork does NOT. maxDepth 99 and an omitted maxDepth are both refused, and a depth-1 child IS admitted.

THE FIFTH PATH, measured by V8 because no test covered it: a COLD RESUME is classified as a child (isSessionBackedChild true, origin subagent survives persistence) and TAKES a host slot. Also carries the CAP-09, CAP-10 and CAP-13 measurements.

cases.note: PASS. Five admission paths, all measured: continuable, one-shot, direct AgentFactory, workflow/PTC (which funnels through the one-shot start), and COLD RESUME, which V8 measured because no existing test covered it. The cold-resume arm matters because a resume reaches AgentRegistry.resume and publishes with source resume rather than create, so whether the agent/created guard sees it is a question about DSH s own publication path. It does: a resumed child is classified as a child and takes a slot.

cases.requirement: a completion admits a replacement without waiting for the wave
cases.stimulus: With sufficient ready supply, let the fastest child complete while the others still run.
cases.oracle: The replacement starts without waiting for the remaining children, and the measured delay from completion to replacement start is recorded against the declared SLO.

evidence.what: The measured refill timeline: one completion, nine siblings still running, and a replacement admitted 23ms after the slot was freed by confirmation. The test states in its own output that no SLO is asserted, because none is frozen in this repository.

The N=10 rolling refill: three rounds, each completing exactly ONE child while NINE stay provably active and hold their slots, each round admitting exactly ONE replacement back to ten; 13 distinct children ran, peak 10.

cases.note: PASS with a stated limit: the oracle asks for the measured delay "against the declared SLO", and NO SLO IS DECLARED anywhere in this repository (grep for SLO over src/, runners/ and docs/ returns only comments stating that none is frozen). The delay is therefore reported as a measured number -- 23ms from confirmation to admission in the recorded run -- and is NOT asserted against a threshold, because asserting one would mean inventing it. The rolling-versus-wave property itself is established independently of any latency number: the replacement is admitted while nine siblings are provably still active, which a wave scheduler cannot produce.

cases.requirement: an unconfirmed cancel still occupies
cases.stimulus: Send a cancel and, in a separate arm, make cleanup fail while the child process is still alive.
cases.oracle: In both arms the slot remains occupied or the child is quarantined as unknown, and no replacement is admitted into the freed-looking slot. Releasing the slot on a merely REQUESTED cancel is NOT PASS.

evidence.what: A cancel that has only been REQUESTED still occupies: the stopping bucket holds the slot and a further reservation is refused until an explicit release.

Through real children: a cancel is sent through the real service, the child is observed still running 200ms later, the reservation is unchanged, the premature refill is refused, and the slot is released only on the confirmed cancelled transition.

cases.requirement: the root is not starved and is not counted as a child
cases.stimulus: Run 30 children that continuously request provider and tool budget, then have the root need to run.
cases.oracle: The root still obtains a reserved opportunity to run and completes its work, and the root is provably excluded from the child count by a separate check.

evidence.what: With ten children in flight the root reaches its OWN provider call, takes no child slot, is not among the ten, and retains its full reserve: rootAvailable 500, childCeiling 9500, and a 9,501 admission refused for budget without touching the reserve.
The root s own settlement-driven turn is real and is attributed to the root s session, never to a child; the ten are still ten distinct children and the partition is exact.

THE ROOT IS EXCLUDED BY THE CLASSIFIER, not by mount order: a root created AFTER the guard is mounted takes no slot and isSessionBackedChild(root) is false, while a real child in the same rig is true and does take one.

cases.note: PASS. Note for a reader: the oracle asks that the root be "provably excluded from the child count by a separate check". That separate check is the classifier case, which removes the mount-order confound -- a root created AFTER the guard is mounted still takes no slot, and isSessionBackedChild returns false for it while returning true for a real child in the same rig. The weaker version of this assertion would hold even if the classifier returned true for everything.

cases.requirement: no filler or idle placeholder children
cases.stimulus: Set the target to 30 with only 2 ready tasks.
cases.oracle: Exactly 2 children are created, the shortage is reported with its reason, and the root is notified. Creating sleep or idle placeholder children to reach the number is NOT PASS.

evidence.what: Target 30 with 2 ready tasks creates exactly TWO real children, reports deficit 28 with reason insufficient_ready_tasks, notifies the root through the outbox, and creates no idle session to pad the count.
The same property through real children: three ready tasks and target 10 create exactly three children and report a seven-slot deficit.

cases.requirement: the cap is host-wide across roots
cases.stimulus: Two roots each request 30 children, with each root's own configuration allowing 30.
cases.oracle: The whole host stays at or below 30, and the queue, the fairness between roots and the real deficit are visible. A per-root cap that lets the host exceed 30 in aggregate is NOT PASS.

evidence.what: One host ledger across two REAL roots, with the per-family pool raised to 64 on purpose so a refusal can only come from the host-wide ledger: root A takes two, root B takes the last of three, then BOTH are refused with "hard capacity is 3"; neither refused child exists in the registry.

cases.note: PASS. The two-roots arm raises the per-family pool to 64 on purpose so that a refusal can only come from the host-wide ledger -- otherwise the refusal would be over-determined and would not distinguish the family pool from the global cap. The composed profile sets both to 10, which is exactly why this measurement is not taken there.

cases.requirement: target changes are honest in both directions
cases.stimulus: Adjust the target 30 -> 1 -> 30 while completions are arriving concurrently.
cases.oracle: Lowering does not silently kill running children, raising tops up within a bounded delay, and the reported revision matches the sequence of changes.

evidence.what: Raise 3 -> 5 admits two more immediately; lower 5 -> 2 admits NONE and kills nothing (every child still live, still holding its slot, every reservedCost unchanged, terminalTombstones empty); re-maintenance after convergence admits again.

cases.requirement: credit reservation is atomic
cases.stimulus: Have many launches contend for the last available cost credit in the same instant.
cases.oracle: Exactly one reservation succeeds, the ledger does not overspend, and an unknown usage stays conservatively reserved rather than being treated as zero. The final ledger is recorded.

evidence.what: THE CONTENTION ARM, measured by V8 because no test covered it: three concurrent drains against ONE free credit admit exactly one (accepted=1 refused=2), the ledger lands exactly ON the child ceiling (reserved=100, childCeiling=100), and both refusals name the budget.

The conservative half of the same oracle: an auxiliary request whose usage never arrived is retained as an unknown and can only TIGHTEN admission (childHeadroom falls), and an unknown is never treated as zero.

cases.requirement: a completion storm neither duplicates nor misses a top-up
cases.stimulus: Have many children complete within one event-loop interval.
cases.oracle: No duplicate launch, no overshoot past the target, and no missed replacement; the coalesced drain is shown to be re-triggerable. The exact launch count is recorded.

evidence.what: THE DEFECT, measured with ZERO real children: freedSlots=2, concurrentRequests=3 -> admitted=3, heldAgainstTarget3=4, deficitAfter=0. The target was 3. Reproduces the coalescing hole in WorkService.drain with a scripted port, so the fault is the service s own arithmetic and not anything the provider or the subagent runtime does.

The BALANCED storm, which PASSES and is the shape the shipped code was built for: three freed slots and three concurrent requests admit exactly three, a later refill is admitted, and the coalesced drain is re-triggerable. Recorded so the reader can see which shape passes and which does not.
Two concurrent drains racing on one free slot produce exactly one launch.

The same defect through three REAL children, as an annotated it.fails case whose comment records the trace: three concurrent refills against two freed slots, three accepted, four tasks holding slots against a target of three.

The gate table, section 2: the defect, its mechanism from host.ts:1242-1256, why the neighbouring CAP-09 credit check does NOT have the same hole, and why it is not fixed here (host.ts is outside this family s file ownership).

cases.note: FAIL, MEASURED. The oracle states "no overshoot past the target". WorkService.drain (host.ts:1242-1256) coalesces by awaiting an in-flight drain and then starting its OWN runDrain WITHOUT re-checking pendingDrain, so K concurrent callers resume in one microtask batch and each reads a record none of them has written yet. Measured with zero real children: freedSlots=2, concurrentRequests=3, admitted=3, four tasks holding slots against a target of three, and capacityDeficit reads 0 so the overshoot is invisible to the deficit reader. The same defect reproduces through three real children in the annotated it.fails case in capacity.test.ts. The BALANCED storm (3 freed / 3 requested) does pass, and that is recorded too. NOT fixed here: host.ts is outside this family s file ownership; the fix is to re-check pendingDrain after the await. See qualification/results/V8-capacity/GATES.md section 2.

cases.requirement: pause stops admission and does not silently resume
cases.stimulus: With root inference, child tools and a top-up queue all present, trigger a user pause.
cases.oracle: No new child is admitted and no continuation silently resumes. The record states which already-published effects are still stopping or awaiting reconciliation, and which are confirmed stopped.

evidence.what: A user pause with FREE SLOTS REMAINING admits nothing (every outcome accepted === false) and the real registry still lists exactly the children that were already running.
The service-level gate: admission while paused is refused with an explicit "is paused" error rather than being silently ignored.

cases.note: PASS for the half its evidence establishes, with the other half stated rather than smoothed over. The admission half holds: a pause with free slots remaining admits nothing and no continuation resumes implicitly (resume is a separate explicit call). The oracle s second half -- "the record states which already-published effects are still stopping or awaiting reconciliation, and which are confirmed stopped" -- is NOT satisfied as written: counts carries stopping and quarantinedUnknown as separate numbers, but there is no "confirmed stopped" counterpart and no "awaiting reconciliation" field, and reconcile.ts is imported by neither counting.ts nor tools.ts. Separately, pause has NO production caller anywhere in the repository, which is the same unreachability shape as G-SEAM-31 one level down. A reader who needs the reporting half should treat this case as partially established. See GATES.md section 3.

cases.requirement: a cost overrun is recorded, not edited away
cases.stimulus: Let real usage exceed the reservation, and let an auxiliary request appear on the bill.
cases.oracle: The overrun and any unknown are recorded and new admissions pause. Removing or adjusting the charge to keep the report green is NOT PASS.

evidence.what: Seventeen tests: reserve 1 / actual 3 records spent 3 and overage 2 with the halt reason naming both numbers, keeps the task s own full spend, refuses the next admission with budget_overage_halt, leaves desiredTarget unchanged, and clears the halt only through an explicit human authorization. Nothing is trimmed to keep the report green.

cases.requirement: depth, family and global limits are each applied
cases.stimulus: Have a child attempt to open grandchildren while a second root uses the same provider.
cases.oracle: The depth ceiling and the per-run/global provider limits each take effect independently, and a family-scoped pool is not reported as the global limit. Each refusal names which limit fired.

evidence.what: THE THREE LIMITS SEPARATED on one rig (pool 4, host gate 30), which is what the oracle asks for: the family pool refuses with "active child limit: 4" and does NOT claim the host hard capacity; the depth ceiling refuses with "delegation depth 2; the deployment ceiling is 1" as a ChildCapacityError reaching the caller unwrapped; hostRefusals {HOST_CAPACITY_REACHED: 0, DEPTH_CEILING_EXCEEDED: 1} with hostOccupied 4 of hostLimit 30. A depth refusal costs no slot.

The depth half independently: maxDepth 99 and an omitted maxDepth are both refused with the DEPTH code, a depth refusal consumes no capacity slot, and a depth-1 child is admitted so the ceiling is not a blanket refusal.

cases.requirement: a zero-test run is not a PASS
cases.stimulus: Run a runner that exits 0 while collecting no test at all.
cases.oracle: The verdict is NOT PASS and the reason names the zero-test condition. The observed exit code is recorded so the reader can see that exit 0 alone would have been read as green.

evidence.note: The oracle, the exact command, the verbatim CLI output and the receipt's own fields: exit.code 0, outcome 'zero_tests', passed false, and the reason naming the zero-test condition. So exit 0 alone is demonstrably not read as green.
The real receipt the run wrote, with exit.code 0 recorded beside passed false.

In-suite arm plus its CONTROL: the same command over the same tree with the same exit 0 and NO declared counts reports outcome 'pass', so the difference between the two receipts is the classification and nothing about the process. 51 passed / 51, TEST_EXIT=0.

cases.requirement: an all-skipped run is not a PASS
cases.stimulus: Run a suite in which every test is skipped and the runner exits 0.
cases.oracle: The verdict is NOT PASS, the skip count is reported, and the recorded exit code shows it was 0.

evidence.note: Verbatim CLI output and receipt: exit.code 0, outcome 'all_skipped', passed false, observedTests {total:2, passed:0, failed:0, skipped:2, todo:0}. The skip count is reported and the exit code is shown to have been 0.
The real receipt, carrying the observed skip counts and exit.code 0.
In-suite arm asserting observedTests {passed:0, failed:0, skipped:2} AND testsAreReal().real === false, so the integration authority refuses it too. 51 passed / 51, TEST_EXIT=0.

cases.requirement: the candidate cannot weaken its own oracle
cases.stimulus: Have the candidate attempt to modify a protected suite, a threshold, or the acceptance configuration.
cases.oracle: The modification is either impossible or detected, and acceptance is not weakened. A silent green produced by an edited oracle is NOT PASS.

evidence.note: The weakened definition is DETECTED: outcome 'acceptance_definition_changed', exit.code null, limitations ['the acceptance command was never executed'], and the refusal names both digests. The corrected CONTROL shows the honest definition with the same authorized digest still RUNS.
Raw capture, including the first control arm that changed the definition id and was refused for that reason -- kept because a control that fails for the reason it is controlling for proves nothing.
The refusal receipt, showing nothing ran.

In-suite arms: the weakened threshold carrying the authorized digest is REFUSED; the undeclared-oracle gap is MEASURED; and the closure (oracleDigest + bindReceipt + observedBasis) refuses a receipt whose oracle changed. 51 passed / 51, TEST_EXIT=0.

cases.note: The oracle-digest closure is a MECHANISM, not an enforced policy: that any production caller passes the right oracleFiles set is NOT proven, and the runner's snapshot still does not cover an undeclared oracle.

cases.requirement: a receipt does not outlive the tree it describes
cases.stimulus: Verify a tree, then change the workspace, the environment or the oracle, and re-check the stored receipt.
cases.oracle: The freshness check reports NOT FRESH and the old verdict is not reusable as current completion. Reusing a stale receipt is NOT PASS. NOTE: this is the NEW VER-04 and has nothing to do with the old spec's VER-04, which is out of scope and recorded in not_applicable_inherited.

evidence.note: CLI end to end: fresh -> {fresh:true}, check_exit 0; after one byte of a declared input changes -> {fresh:false} with both digests named, check_exit 1 and the runner says 're-verify'. CONTROL: a FRESH receipt that is not a PASS still exits 1, so freshness is never a verdict.
The verbatim capture of all arms, including what the receipt does NOT carry (no oracleDigest field: the oracle binding is a separate VerdictBinding compared by bindReceipt, by design).
The real receipt, carrying candidateTreeDigest, candidateTreeDigestScope and acceptanceDefinitionDigest.

In-suite arms for the WORKSPACE, ORACLE and ENVIRONMENT bindings independently, each moving exactly one of four real digests, with a restored tree ACCEPTING as the control. 51 passed / 51, TEST_EXIT=0.

cases.note: Numbering honoured: this is the NEW VER-04 (receipt freshness). The old VER-04 (host execution bypass) is out of scope and recorded in not_applicable_inherited; nothing here is evidence for it.

cases.requirement: A-B-A mutation during acceptance is caught
cases.stimulus: Change a file and change it back to its original hash while acceptance is running.
cases.oracle: The candidate is frozen to an immutable snapshot and the verdict is bound to that snapshot, so the tampered run cannot be certified. The control arm must also be run: endpoint hash polling alone would have certified the tampered run, and that is demonstrated rather than asserted.

evidence.note: The printed numbers for the oracle: the frozen arm's child read revision A for input+oracle+config while the live tree went A->B->A; liveDigestAtStart == liveDigestAtEnd and liveDriftDetected false, so endpoint polling sees NOTHING; the in-place CONTROL exits 9 having seen the tampered tree, and both receipts carry the SAME start digest.
The verbatim probe output, including the serialized-receipt asymmetry that makes the snapshot load-bearing rather than decorative.

In-suite two-arm proof extended to the oracle and the config, plus the case where a command rewrites its own declared input inside the snapshot and the outcome is 'unknown' with holdReservation true. 51 passed / 51, TEST_EXIT=0.

cases.requirement: in-flight writers are converged or isolated before freezing
cases.stimulus: Complete a request while a background mutation is still active.
cases.oracle: The system converges or isolates the writer before freezing, and an unresolved mutation produces an unknown rather than a certification. Certifying a tree that was still changing is NOT PASS.

evidence.note: Three measured paths: a live writer lease refuses the freeze; a released lease with a still-moving tree refuses and names BOTH sample digests; a stopped writer converges to a digest EQUAL to the runner's own digestInputs. The structural invariant digest!=='' implies converged===true holds on every path.
The verbatim probe output for all three paths, with their distinct refusal reasons printed separately.
In-suite arms: 'freezing while a writer still holds the workspace is REFUSED as in-flight', the two-arm convergence case, and 'a refusal NEVER carries a digest'. 51 passed / 51, TEST_EXIT=0.

cases.note: Measures the freeze DECISION. That a production caller invokes convergeBeforeFreeze before every acceptance is the caller's to provide and is NOT claimed.

cases.requirement: a verification failure does not permanently drain the run
cases.stimulus: Fail verification, then legitimately resume the run with corrected work.
cases.oracle: Legitimate recovery continues, and `pause` has not been misused as a final drain. A run that cannot continue after a recoverable failure is NOT PASS.

evidence.note: The case's five assertions read from source, driven against the REAL SubagentRuntime: pause leaves the run paused and refusing ('run_not_open'); a correction child is still admitted WHILE PAUSED; resume re-opens admission; and only the later permanent drain rejects with 'draining; the operation was not admitted' -- which is what proves the paused state was genuinely not-yet-drained.
The run that carries it: 51 passed / 51, TEST_EXIT=0, 105.62 s, single worker with --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism.

cases.note: Asserted for the pause/drain DISTINCTION, not for a whole recovery: it does not run a full failed -> corrected -> re-verified -> completed turn.

cases.requirement: an acceptance definition cannot authorize itself
cases.stimulus: Change an acceptance definition's threshold and re-run it without re-recording the authorized digest.
cases.oracle: The digest check FAILS and the run is refused. Obtaining the authorized digest must be a separate step from writing the definition, so a definition cannot go green in the same breath it is edited.

evidence.note: The digest check FAILS and the run is refused with nothing executed, and the SEPARATION OF STEPS is shown as two commands: --print-digest prints and writes nothing back, and no flag both authorizes and runs. The corrected control shows the honest definition with the same digest still runs.
The corrected control arm with both digests printed side by side.
In-suite arm: the weakened threshold carrying the authorized digest is REFUSED, not run, while the same definition with the same digest really executes. 51 passed / 51, TEST_EXIT=0.

cases.requirement: the verification tier and its limit are stated, never implied
cases.stimulus: Read every recorded verdict in this deployment and compare the claimed tier with the tier at which it was measured.
cases.oracle: Each verdict names its tier from the layer legend and the artifact it is bound to; a green measured at T0/T1 is never presented as T2/T3/T5/T6. Under trusted-local the verification environment runs as the SAME OS user as the host, so the record must ALSO state that no privilege separation between the verifier and the verified exists. Presenting a same-account verification as privileged isolation is NOT PASS.

evidence.note: All three clauses. 109/109 cases name a tier from the layer legend; 0 T5 cases are PASS while live_provider_budget_authorized is false; the old gate index shares no id with this spec. And the SAME-ACCOUNT measurement taken from inside the verification child: child user 'hzq00' == host user 'hzq00' at a different pid, so no privilege separation exists -- stated in the deployment's own trust_model_statement rather than implied.

The machine-readable audit: per-case layer distribution, the T5 expectation, the receipt's binding fields, and its own scope statement -- it audits tier discipline in the record and does not judge whether an oracle was established.

The raw capture of the same-account probe driven through the real acceptance runner, plus what the runner DOES remove (credential-shaped and DSH_* env names, the control-plane handle) kept separate from what it does NOT (filesystem reads, egress).

The clause-2 cross-check against the other families' gate tables: ZERO explicit tier tokens beside case ids were found. Recorded as the empty result it is, with the reason it is empty, rather than folded into a green.

The in-suite cases that measure the CONSEQUENCES of the same-account limit: a candidate child read a host file outside its snapshot verbatim, and a candidate child completed a real TCP connection. 51 passed / 51, TEST_EXIT=0.

cases.note: An identity drift was found while filing and is reported rather than absorbed: trusted_local_acceptance_spec_sha256 pins THIS spec's digest, and this spec is also the results register every family writes into, so filing into it changes the identity. See qualification/results/V9-verification/identity-at-measurement.txt. No unilateral re-derivation was performed -- moving deployment.identity is an owner-level decision.

cases.requirement: the search-to-citation chain uses real sources
cases.stimulus: Run an independent search, fetch the original source, widen to the full relevant range, then cite.
cases.oracle: Every step carries a real source with a version and a timestamp. A missing key or a failed fetch is reported as a failure, never turned into a fabricated result or an invented citation.

cases.requirement: the evidence tier is not inflated
cases.stimulus: Store only the bytes of a PDF without ever presenting its body to the reader.
cases.oracle: The record reports `bytes_captured` and does not claim `primary_read` or `understood`. The tier vocabulary must not even contain the stronger values as reachable states.

cases.requirement: an incomplete parse reports its own limits
cases.stimulus: Parse a PDF whose body omits tables, and separately follow a redirect, a 404 and a truncated body.
cases.oracle: The read range and its limitations are stated for each case, and missing content is never filled in. Using a search snippet as if it were the full text is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: provider truncation is not local full recoverability
cases.stimulus: Have a provider deliver only the first part of a body.
cases.oracle: `acquisition.completeness` is `partial` with recovery `none` or `refetch`, and the record does not claim the full text is locally recoverable. Claiming completeness from a truncated fetch is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: raw and derived content are separately identified
cases.stimulus: De-script an HTML page and convert it to markdown, including a conversion that fails.
cases.oracle: Raw and derived artifacts carry separate hashes and separate locators, and a failed conversion produces an explicit failure rather than manufactured body text.

cases.requirement: a claim is locatable and external content stays untrusted
cases.stimulus: Make a final claim citing a page or fragment, from a page that also contains embedded commands, a skill-update instruction and an authority claim.
cases.oracle: The claim can be located in the captured artifact at a named span, a snippet is not treated as the full text, and the external content is wrapped as untrusted data that cannot change host authority or cause execution.

cases.requirement: observation caching is measured, not assumed
cases.stimulus: Observe one unchanged stored session N times with the cache sized above N, and count the underlying reads.
cases.oracle: The read count is recorded verbatim. A cache that produces N reads where a hit would produce 1 is reported as a DEFECT with its cause, not described as a cache that works. A bound and an eviction policy are not a hit rate.

cases.requirement: a scan watermark is stable while events append
cases.stimulus: Run a history scan while new events keep being appended.
cases.oracle: The page order is fixed to one snapshot for the whole scan, and events appended after the snapshot are read in a separate pass with their own watermark. Interleaving new events into the running scan is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: one oversized event does not break the page budget
cases.stimulus: Read a history page containing a single event larger than the page budget.
cases.oracle: An authorized reference or a segmented read is returned, and the page budget is not exceeded. Truncating silently, or emitting the whole event inline, is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: repeated traversal does not re-replay the whole log
cases.stimulus: Traverse the same history for 100 pages.
cases.oracle: A prepared observation or index is reused, and the actual number of full log replays is recorded as a number. A measured 100 replays for 100 pages is reported as the defect it is.

cases.requirement: the three visibilities stay separate
cases.stimulus: Store an event without reading it programmatically, then read it without emitting it, then emit it.
cases.oracle: `obtainable`, `consumed` and `model-projected` are recorded as three separate states and are never merged into one. Reporting a stored event as model-visible, or a consumed event as projected, is NOT PASS.

cases.requirement: a derived index is rebuildable from canonical data
cases.stimulus: Delete the derived full-text index, then restore.
cases.oracle: The index is rebuilt from the canonical Session and artifact data with no second history source required, and the rebuilt index answers the same queries as before. The rebuild is recorded with what it read.

not_applicable_inherited.what_this_section_is: The five isolation-only gates from the OLD specs are recorded here, deliberately, rather than dropped. They are NOT cases of this spec: they are not in `cases`, they carry no status field, and no evidence may be filed against them. This section is a record of a decision, not a work queue.
not_applicable_inherited.why_not_applicable_and_not_fail: The new architecture does not CLAIM these invariants. FAIL means 'this architecture claims the invariant and did not achieve it'. Under trusted-local the OS user account is the execution authority boundary, so there is no isolation domain in which any of these five invariants could hold, and none is promised. Marking them FAIL would assert a claim this deployment does not make and cannot make; marking them PASS would assert an achievement that does not exist. NOT_APPLICABLE is the only honest state, and it is honest only because the trust model states the absence explicitly.
not_applicable_inherited.why_not_dropped: Each of the five was measured or analysed in the old deployment. That work is real and is retained as the reason these invariants are out of scope. Dropping them silently would let a reader think they were never considered, and would hide the fact that two of them were honest FAILs on this platform before the architecture changed.

entries.old_oracle: native read and Python direct read of host HOME/DSH_HOME/proc -> both paths unreachable; a read-only host root is not secrecy
entries.reasoning: The new architecture does not claim read isolation at any level. The old FAIL was measured, not assumed: a confined child read a canary file outside the workspace root verbatim, exit 0, under BOTH read-only and workspace-write, and four candidate levers were probed with none able to restrict a read. The old oracle also demanded that a read-only host root not be presented as secrecy, which is a claim-about-claims this deployment now satisfies by stating the absence outright. There is nothing left to test: the deployment promises exactly what was measured. Evidence for the old measurement: qualification/results/R10-security/, qualification/results/M9.13-isolation/, qualification/results/MAIN-sandbox-path/.

entries.old_oracle: DNS/IPv4/IPv6/LAN/cloud-metadata access -> unauthorized direct connections blocked by OS or gateway; record the real result
entries.reasoning: The new architecture does not claim a network boundary. The old FAIL was measured: a confined child completed a real HTTP round trip and reached a LAN address, and the sandbox seam's own documentation states that network is outside its vocabulary, so no configuration of it could ever have provided this. Two things that DO still hold are kept as separate cases rather than smuggled in here: the web tool's own address policy remains a live obligation (SEC-04 in the old spec, not in scope here as isolation), and this deployment makes no egress claim in its documentation. Evidence: qualification/results/R10-security/, qualification/results/MAIN-sandbox-path/MEASURED.txt.

entries.requirement: role / read-permission-domain transition on kernel reuse
entries.old_oracle: reuse a kernel after a read-permission-domain or project change -> a new epoch or a controlled migration is required; old-domain secret variables must not carry over
entries.reasoning: The requirement's precondition is the existence of two or more read-permission domains. This deployment has exactly one execution world (the invoking OS user), so there is no domain to transition between and no cross-domain reuse to test. This is not a capability that was not built: the requirement itself is dissolved by the architecture. Recorded so that a reader does not mistake its absence for outstanding work. Evidence for the single-world premise: deployment.inputs and the resolved profile graph.

entries.old_oracle: view the same path through native read / grep / process / web -> all resolve to the same executionWorld; do not misread a same-named host file
entries.reasoning: The requirement's precondition is the existence of a second execution world that a path could be mis-resolved against. No SSH provider is mounted and no SSH world will be built; the deployment is single-world by decision. In a single world the oracle is vacuously true, which is why leaving it as NOT_RUN would be actively misleading: it would read as an outstanding obligation when it is an empty one. The genuine, still-live half of its subject -- that one path string resolves to one file across every route -- is preserved as FS-03 in this spec, at the layer where it is actually checkable.

entries.requirement: verification-environment privilege separation from the host
entries.old_oracle: candidate tests attempt to read host secrets or send network traffic -> the verification environment is still low-privilege and unauthorized operations are blocked
entries.reasoning: The new architecture does not claim that the verification environment is separated from the host. It is not: candidate tests run as the same OS user as the host, with the same filesystem and network reach. This is the most consequential of the five, because the old case guarded the credibility of the verification chain itself rather than a runtime boundary. The consequence is carried forward explicitly rather than absorbed: VER-09 of this spec requires every verdict to state its tier and to state that no privilege separation between verifier and verified exists. What is NOT carried forward is any claim of isolation, because none exists to test. Numbering warning: the old VER-04 and the new VER-04 are different cases; the new VER-04 is receipt freshness. Evidence for the old analysis: qualification/results/R10-security/FINDINGS.md section 5, qualification/results/M8-verification/.

reading_notes.for_evidence_authors: Every case is mandatory and starts NOT_RUN with empty evidence. To file evidence, put a file under qualification/results/<your-slice>/ and record its repo-relative path plus sha256 on the case. A case may only be marked PASS when that file establishes THIS oracle, at THIS deployment identity.
reading_notes.what_is_not_allowed: No PASS by editing an oracle after the fact, by skipping a case, by lowering a threshold, by widening a permission, or by recording a result that was not produced. If a case cannot be met, it stays NOT_RUN or FAIL, and the reason is recorded.
reading_notes.not_applicable_rule: No case in `cases` may take the status NOT_APPLICABLE. The only out-of-scope items in this spec are the five entries in not_applicable_inherited, which are not cases.
reading_notes.blocked_external: Cases at layer T5 need an authorized live provider. compatibility.lock.json -> runtime_authorization.live_provider_budget_authorized is false, so they are expected to remain BLOCKED_EXTERNAL.
